notes.prov-kamu-kamu: Small steps add up. Like learning a language!
notes.prov-olugalo-olumu: You need others to get things done.
notes.prov-atannayitaayita: Travel and you’ll see the world is wider.

guidebook.intro: Proverbs, **engero**, are the spice of Ganda speech. Elders use them to advise, to settle arguments and to make a point gracefully.

tips.title: Reading a proverb
body: Proverbs use images from daily life: bundles of sticks, teeth, fingers, cooking. Their meaning is never literal. **Kamu kamu gwe muganda** is about patience: a bundle of firewood is gathered one stick at a time.
**Agali awamu ge galuma enyama** and **Olugalo olumu teruta nda** both praise working together.

tips.title: Bringing one in
body: Introduce a proverb with **Nga bwe bagamba** (as they say). To ask about one you hear, say **Olugero luno lutegeeza ki?** (What does this proverb mean?). Using a proverb well will impress any Muganda.

culture.title: Proverbs at ceremonies
body: At a kwanjula or a clan meeting, spokespeople compete with proverbs. A well-placed proverb can win the crowd and settle a point.
